summary: SCHC is a way to squeeze and fragment packets for very low-power, low-bandwidth wireless links. When a large packet is split into pieces, the receiver normally sends acknowledgements after each window of pieces. This document adds a Compound ACK that bundles the bitmaps for several windows into one message, cutting down the number of replies. It updates RFC 8724 and RFC 9363.

eli5.summary: Imagine a friend reading you a long list in small chunks. Instead of saying "got it" after every chunk, you wait a bit and report all the chunks you got in one message. That saves your breath.

questions: how to reduce acknowledgements in schc fragmentation
what is a schc compound ack
how does schc ack-on-error mode work
subtitle: Lets a receiver report missing pieces from several windows in a single reply, saving scarce radio transmissions.

tldr.problem: In SCHC ACK-on-Error mode, the receiver sends one failure ACK per window with losses. On Low-Power Wide Area Networks, every extra reply is costly.
tldr.mechanism: The SCHC Compound ACK is a failure ACK that carries several bitmaps, each tagged with its window number, so one message can report losses in many windows.
tldr.outcome: It reduces the number of ACK transmissions, stays backwards compatible with the RFC 8724 ACK, and rewrites Section 8.4.3 of RFC 8724. It is optional and a Profile decides whether to use it.

today: RFC 9441 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2023. It has not been obsoleted or updated, and it updates RFC 8724 and RFC 9363.

sections.title: Why a Compound ACK
sections.content:
SCHC (Static Context Header Compression) has two parts: header compression, and fragmentation with loss recovery. RFC 8724 defines both, and they can run over the four LPWAN technologies listed in RFC 8376: Sigfox, LoRaWAN, NB-IoT and IEEE 802.15.4w.

In ACK-on-Error mode, a SCHC Packet is cut into tiles of equal size (the last may be smaller), and consecutive tiles are grouped into fixed-size windows. After the All-1 fragment arrives, the receiver reports on exactly one window. If losses span several windows, it sends one failure ACK per window with losses.

This document adds the SCHC Compound ACK to cut those replies. It updates RFC 8724 and the YANG model in RFC 9363.
sections.eli5: Sending a message over a tiny radio is expensive. Instead of sending many short notes saying what was lost, the receiver can send one longer note.

sections.title: The Compound ACK Message Format
sections.content:
A Compound ACK is a failure ACK (C=0) that can hold several bitmaps, each identified by its window number W. It reports only on windows with losses, has a variable size, and might not cover every window with losses. It is distinguishable from the SCHC Receiver-Abort message.

Window numbers need not be contiguous, but the window numbers and their bitmaps MUST be ordered from lowest to highest. If window 0 is reported, it MUST come first and its number goes in the ACK header.

If M or more padding bits would be needed after the last bitmap to fill the last layer two (L2) Word, M bits set to 0 are appended and then padding is applied. Window 0 can only be the first, so these zero bits cannot be mistaken for a window number and they mark the end of the message. If fewer than M padding bits are needed, there is no room for another window, which also signals the end.

Intermediate bitmaps MUST NOT be compressed and MUST be of size WINDOW_SIZE. Only the last bitmap MAY use the Compressed Bitmap format, and only if the technology-specific Profile says so. A sender that receives invalid window numbers, such as duplicates or windows not sent yet, MUST discard the whole message.
sections.eli5: The note lists each window that had missing pieces, in order, with a little checklist for each. A special run of zeros tells the sender the note is over.

sections.title: How Sender and Receiver Behave
sections.content:
Section 3.2.1 of this document replaces Section 8.4.3 of RFC 8724. The Compound ACK is a generalisation of the old ACK, which reports one window, so it is backwards compatible. If a receiver sends a Compound ACK covering several windows and the sender resends tiles only from the first one, the receiver can assume the sender does not support it and fall back to one window per ACK.

Receiver: on an All-0 fragment the receiver MAY return a Compound ACK starting from the lowest-numbered window with missing tiles, depending on conditions such as network state, sender buffer size and application delay. The criteria are not specified. On an All-1 fragment or a SCHC ACK REQ it MUST return one if it knows of windows with missing tiles. Otherwise it returns an ACK for the highest-numbered window it has tiles for, or for window 0 if it has no tiles.

Sender: it MUST listen for Compound ACKs after an All-1 fragment or an ACK REQ, and MUST resend all tiles of every window reported missing. It can advance to later windows before earlier ones are confirmed, so sender and receiver work in a decoupled fashion. The Attempts counter and Retransmission Timer limit retries, and when the counter reaches MAX_ACK_REQUESTS the sender MUST send a Sender-Abort.
sections.eli5: The receiver keeps track of which pieces are missing. When asked, it sends one list of everything missing, and the sender resends exactly those pieces.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.content:
The RFC shows a SCHC Packet fragmented into 14 tiles, with N=3, WINDOW_SIZE=7 and M=2. Two fragments are lost: one in window 0 (FCN=2) and one in window 1 (FCN=1). The receiver does not answer the All-0 fragment, and after the All-1 fragment (with the RCS) the integrity check fails, so it sends a single Compound ACK with bitmap 1111011 for window 0 and 1111101 for window 1.

The sender resends the two missing tiles, the integrity check succeeds, and the receiver replies with an ordinary ACK with C=1. Only one Compound ACK was needed instead of two failure ACKs.
sections.eli5: Two pieces went missing in different groups. One note listed both, the sender resent them, and everything was complete.

sections.title: YANG Data Model Extension
sections.content:
The document extends the SCHC YANG model of RFC 9363 with a module named ietf-schc-compound-ack. It augments the ACK-on-Error fragmentation mode with two leaves: bitmap-format, which selects either the RFC 8724 bitmap (the default) or the compound ACK format, and last-bitmap-compression, a boolean that defaults to true.

A Profile must now also state whether the Compound ACK message is used and whether the compressed bitmap format is used in the last window. This list is appended to the parameters in Appendix D of RFC 8724.
sections.eli5: There is a settings sheet for devices. This adds two switches: use the combined note or not, and shrink the last checklist or not.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The Compound ACK is a message format extension, so the security considerations of RFC 8724 and RFC 9363 apply. For the YANG module, access should go over secure management transports, and writable nodes are sensitive: an attacker who changes the fragmentation mode or Compound ACK usage of other devices may block communication or create extra ACKs. A device must be allowed to modify only its own Rules on the remote SCHC instance, and the requester's identity must be validated.

IANA registered the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-schc-compound-ack and the YANG module name ietf-schc-compound-ack.
sections.eli5: Only the owner of a device should be able to change its settings, otherwise a bad actor could make the radio chatter pointlessly.

viz.caption: MESSAGE SEQUENCE FROM THE RFC EXAMPLE (SIMPLIFIED)

data.title: Compound ACK exchange
data.code:
W=0, FCN=6..0 sent, FCN=2 lost -> bitmap 1111011
(no ACK)
W=1, FCN=6..1 sent, FCN=1 lost
W=1, FCN=7 + RCS -> integrity check: failure
<- Compound ACK [C=0, W=0 bitmap 1111011, W=1 bitmap 1111101]
W=0, FCN=2 resent
W=1, FCN=1 resent -> integrity check: success
<- ACK, W=1, C=1

viz.caption: COMPOUND ACK LAYOUT, LOSSES IN WINDOWS 00 AND 01
